Thought: I need to analyze each statement about snake venom and determine which one(s) are false.

A. Neurotoxic snake venoms can have a presynaptic and postsynaptic effect, depending on the type of venom.
This is true. Snake neurotoxins can act at different sites in the nervous system - some affect the presynaptic terminals (preventing neurotransmitter release) while others act postsynaptically (blocking receptors).

B. Snake venoms are exclusively proteins and peptides.
This is likely false. While snake venoms are primarily composed of proteins and peptides, they also contain other components like enzymes, glycoproteins, lipids, and small organic compounds.

C. The poisons of the European poisonous snakes are neurotoxins and proteases.
This appears to be true. European venomous snakes like vipers typically have venoms containing both neurotoxic components and proteolytic enzymes.

D. The venom of the adder is fatal in about 50% of those bitten.
This is false. The European adder (Vipera berus) has a relatively low fatality rate, much lower than 50%. Untreated mortality rates are typically less than 1%.
